chains.note: The extractor is committed (it is our code, not third-party text) so anyone holding the archived HTML can regenerate the exact analyzed text and check it against these hashes. chains.extractor: pdftotext (poppler / Glyph & Cog) version 4.00, external binary
chains.note: STRICTLY WEAKER THAN GRADE A and used only where the publisher ships no HTML full text. The chain is reproducible — same PDF bytes, same tool version, same recorded command, same output — but it depends on an external tool version rather than on a hashed file in this repository, so it cannot be verified from the repo alone. Each sidecar records the full command including the -nopgbrk flag (without it pdftotext injects page-break form feeds that defeat the line anchors) and the start/stop anchors used. No committed repo script reads PDFs; adding one was out of scope for this run.

labelingSheets.purpose: Peer-review artifacts with an empty VERDICT column, one per source. Section A grades every mapping (CORRECT/FALSE-POSITIVE), section B every unmapped claim-like passage (OK-NO-CANON/MISS), section C every passage the domain gate set aside (OK/SHOULD-HAVE-BEEN-RETAINED). A graded set becomes the fixture the threshold-calibration pass needs — today's thresholds were authored by judgment and never fitted to labelled data, which is what coverage.provisional records.

acquisition.notes: THE C2 PRIMARY, and the verification materially weakened the claim. Independently confirmed against this archive: n=2,969 US adults 18+, gathered by Qualtrics through 'existing sample panels... screened based on a quota sampling framework' — an OPT-IN QUOTA PANEL, not a probability sample, with no published MOE — plus 'an additional oversample of 1,000 individuals aged 18-29'. The headline figures use the perfect tense and are therefore LIFETIME-EVER items, not current use: 19% of adults 'reporting that they have chatted with an AI system meant to simulate a romantic partner', and '31% young adult men / 23% young adult women'. The 21% preference figure has a USER denominator, not a sample denominator: 'Of those who chatted with AI systems to simulate romantic partners, over 1 in 5 (21%) agreed that they preferred AI communication over engaging with a real person.' The instrument contains no current-relationship-status item at all. The report also links companion use to higher depression and loneliness, cross-sectionally, so direction is unknown.

acquisition.notes: THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE for C10's causal step. Pew, n=6,204, American Trends Panel Wave 154 — a probability panel. It found NO sex gap in partner reliance itself: men and women are about equally likely to say they would lean on a spouse or partner. The sex gap is in the BREADTH of other channels, not in partner concentration. This cuts against the naive sole-channel mechanism, and is the reason C10's answer is a three-way split rather than a confirmation.
